title: MSI mode bench
intro: Follow the procedure in the RigPolice article: https://rigpolice.com/system/articles/enable-msi-mode/ . The reboots, the settle wait and the checks between runs were done by the article's test runner; you do them by hand. `msi-bench.ps1` records the interrupt mode of every PCI device, ISR and DPC time per driver from a kernel trace, and a stall probe that counts every gap of 2 us or more in a spinning thread on a chosen CPU. The Superposition load below is the GPU-bound load for it.
needs: Run one interrupt-mode state per series (stock, then after `msi-mode-utility.ps1`, with a reboot between). For `-Background` you also need Unigine Superposition 1.1 installed (the load below) and a USB SSD with a 1 GiB file of real data. Create it once, in PowerShell, with `$r = New-Object System.Random 1; $b = New-Object byte[] 64MB; $f = [System.IO.File]::Create('<path on the USB SSD>'); 1..16 | ForEach-Object { $r.NextBytes($b); $f.Write($b, 0, $b.Length) }; $f.Dispose()` (16 blocks of 64 MiB of pseudo-random data from `System.Random` seeded with 1).
run: `.\msi-bench.ps1 -Phase stock -Load superposition -PresentMon <path to PresentMon-2.6.0-x64.exe> -Device dxgkrnl.sys,HDAudBus.sys,Wdf01000.sys`, then the same with `-Phase msi`. To run the same tone and SSD reads as the article, add `-Background tone,usb-read -UsbReadFile <path of the 1 GiB file>` to the Superposition command (admin shell). Without a load, `-Seconds` sets the window and `-Cpu 0,5` picks the probe CPUs (a load takes its window from the recipe, so `-Seconds` is refused with `-Load`). `-Device` takes the drivers whose interrupts you care about: a 5 s pre-trace finds the CPU that takes most of each driver's ISRs and the probe runs there too. A WDDM GPU logs its ISR as `dxgkrnl.sys`, not as the vendor driver, and `Wdf01000.sys` groups every KMDF device (USB host controller, GPIO). The result holds a histogram of the gaps per probe and `msi-bench-<phase>-stalls.csv` lists every gap of 1 ms or more. Results go next to the script, or to `-OutDir`.
touch: one temporary ETW session named "NT Kernel Logger" that it starts and stops itself (twice with `-Device`: the pre-trace and the main trace), for `-Load` PresentMon with its own ETW session named `rigpolice-bench`, the stall-probe threads, and with `-Background` a 440 Hz tone at -40 dBFS on the default output and an unbuffered read loop over `-UsbReadFile`
game: For `-Load` start the bench before the load: it waits for the load's process and, when the recipe names a start line, for that line in the game log, then waits the load pause and captures frame times with PresentMon while the kernel trace and the probes run. On a load with a fixed route the `-Device` pre-trace runs inside the load pause, so the window stays on the route. Do not touch the PC until it prints the result.
record: `msi-bench.ps1` adds the interrupt mode of every PCI device, the stall probe per CPU (histogram, percentiles, total stalled time, the devices behind each CPU), the trace clock type, the CPU picked per `-Device` driver next to the CPU the main trace shows for it, and, with `-Load`, the load build, whether the installed video config matches the shipped one (mismatched key names only), the names of launch flags outside the recipe (names only, no values), the frame statistics and the count of frames PresentMon lost to a present event buffer overflow (`presentMon.overflowedPresents`; a run that lost any is rejected). `loadWindow` gives the seconds from the load start to the start and to the end of the capture window; on a load with a fixed route a window that ends past the route rejects the run. With `-Background`, the result adds `background`: for the tone its frequency, level, the default playback device name and the PCI controller it sits behind, for the SSD reads the bytes read, wraps, seconds and MiB/s (a read error rejects the run). With `-Load`, `systemCpu` adds the whole-system CPU time over the same window (`windowSeconds`, `busySeconds`, `idleSeconds`, `logicalCpus`), read from the OS at the same two points, so work from processes that start and exit inside the window still shows. Each driver row carries the summed ISR and DPC time (`isrTotalUs`, `dpcTotalUs`). The device table names each PCI device and its driver, because the interrupt mode per device is the measurement.
